title: Locksmith Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual, Fortnightly, and After-Tax Pay
description: Learn how to convert a locksmith salary from hourly to annual, including casual loading, super, and tax. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman Pay Calculator for award rates.
salarySummary: A full-time locksmith on the National Minimum Wage earns $26.44 per hour, or $52,270 annually for 38 hours per week, before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a locksmith in Australia?
faqs.a: The minimum hourly rate for a locksmith depends on the applicable modern award. As a baseline, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. Locksmiths are typically covered by the Manufacturing and Associated Industries and Occupations Award 2020 or a similar award, which may set higher minimum rates. You can check the exact classification rate using the Fair Work Ombudsman Pay Calculator or the Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a locksmith salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For example, if the base rate is $26.44 per hour, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour. This loading is paid on all ordinary hours worked. Superannuation is calculated on the total ordinary earnings, including the casual loading.

faqs.q: How much super is paid on a locksmith salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a full-time locksmith earning $52,270 per year, the employer would contribute an additional $6,272.40 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Locksmith Salary: From Hourly to Annual

If you’re a locksmith or considering the trade, knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and after-tax pay is essential. Whether you’re negotiating a new job, comparing offers, or planning your budget, this guide walks you through the conversion using the standard 38-hour week, casual loading, superannuation, and the 2026–27 tax rates.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay is calculated as:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a full-time week of 38 hours, which is the standard under the National Employment Standards. If you work part-time or overtime, adjust the hours accordingly. For example, a permanent locksmith on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) earns:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,270.24 per year**

This figure is before tax and before super. The same formula works for any hourly rate – just plug in your award rate or agreed wage.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour) is the legal floor. However, most locksmiths are covered by a modern award, such as the Manufacturing and Associated Industries and Occupations Award 2020. Award rates are often higher and include classification-based pay levels. You can find the exact rate for your role using the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or the Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database.

> **Fair Work Commission** provides downloadable spreadsheets of minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each award.

> **Fair Work Ombudsman** offers a Pay Calculator to check your minimum entitlements.

### Casual Loading: Adding 25% on Top

If you work as a casual locksmith, you are entitled to a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. **Do not include the loading in the base rate you enter into a calculator** – it should be added separately. For example:

- Base rate: $26.44/hour
- Casual loading (25%): $6.61/hour
- Casual rate: $33.05/hour

Using the casual rate in the annual formula:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = **$65,342.80 per year**

This is the gross pay before tax and super. For more on how loading works, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation at 12% of your ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026). This is **on top of** your gross pay – it is not deducted from your salary. For the permanent locksmith earning $52,270:

- Super contribution: $52,270 × 12% = $6,272.40
- Total cost to employer: $58,542.64

The super guarantee has a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. If your ordinary earnings exceed that, super is capped. Learn more on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Practical View

Most employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay:

**Weekly pay × 2**

For the permanent locksmith:

- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72
- Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = **$2,009.44**

For the casual locksmith:

- Weekly: $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90
- Fortnightly: $1,255.90 × 2 = **$2,511.80**

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates (with the full tax-free threshold) and the 2% Medicare levy, here’s an estimate of take-home pay for the permanent locksmith earning $52,270:

- Tax-free threshold: $0 – $18,200 → $0 tax
- Next bracket (15%): $18,201 – $45,000 → tax on $26,800 = $4,020
- Next bracket (30%): $45,001 – $52,270 → tax on $7,270 = $2,181
- Total tax: $6,201
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,270): $1,045.40
- Total deductions: $7,246.40
- **Annual take-home: $45,023.84**

Fortnightly take-home: approximately $1,732 (before any HELP or surcharges).

For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Using the Hourly to Annual Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates annual gross, super, tax, and take-home pay. Remember: if you are casual, tick the loading checkbox – do not type a rate that already includes the 25% loading.

### Key Points to Remember

- The formula **hourly × hours × 52** gives annual gross.
- Always check your award rate – the National Minimum Wage is the minimum, not necessarily your rate.
- Casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate.
- Super is 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings, up to the cap.
- Tax estimates use the 2026–27 scale with Medicare levy; your situation may differ if you have HELP debt or salary sacrifice.

For more resources, visit our [reference tables](/data) or [average pay](/topics/average-pay) pages.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
